channel.title: RomNYC - NYC Facts
channel.description: Interesting facts about New York City for the RomNYC webcam ticker.

item.title: New York City has five boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island.
Queens is New York City's largest borough by land area.
Brooklyn is New York City's most populous borough.
Manhattan is New York City's smallest borough by land area.
The Bronx is the only NYC borough located primarily on the mainland.
Staten Island is New York City's southernmost borough.
New York City was originally settled by the Dutch as New Amsterdam.
New Amsterdam was renamed New York after the English took control in 1664.
New York City was the first capital of the United States under the Constitution.
George Washington was inaugurated as president at Federal Hall in New York City in 1789.
Federal Hall once stood on Wall Street in Lower Manhattan.
Wall Street takes its name from a defensive wall built by the Dutch.
Broadway is the only major Manhattan street that runs diagonally through the island.
Times Square was originally known as Longacre Square.
Longacre Square was renamed Times Square in 1904.
Times Square was named after The New York Times moved its headquarters there.
The first New Year's Eve celebration in Times Square took place in 1904.
Central Park opened to the public in 1858.
Central Park covers about 843 acres.
Central Park is larger than the country of Monaco.
The Mall is one of Central Park's most recognizable tree-lined promenades.
Bethesda Fountain is one of Central Park's best-known landmarks.
Bow Bridge is one of Central Park's most photographed bridges.
Belvedere Castle sits on one of the highest points in Central Park.
Strawberry Fields in Central Park is a memorial to John Lennon.
The Empire State Building opened in 1931.
The Empire State Building has 102 floors.
The Empire State Building was the world's tallest building when it opened.
The Chrysler Building opened in 1930.
The Chrysler Building briefly held the title of world's tallest building in 1930.
One World Trade Center is 1,776 feet tall to the top of its spire.
The height of One World Trade Center references the year 1776.
The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States.
The Statue of Liberty was dedicated in 1886.
The Statue of Liberty stands on Liberty Island.
The Statue of Liberty is made primarily of copper.
The Statue of Liberty turned green because of the natural oxidation of its copper exterior.
The Statue of Liberty's tablet bears the date July 4, 1776 in Roman numerals.
The Statue of Liberty's official name is Liberty Enlightening the World.
The Statue of Liberty's crown has seven rays.
The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883.
The Brooklyn Bridge connected Manhattan and Brooklyn when it opened.
The Brooklyn Bridge was the world's longest suspension bridge when it opened.
John A. Roebling conceived the Brooklyn Bridge and served as its chief engineer.
Washington Roebling took over the Brooklyn Bridge project after his father's death.
Emily Warren Roebling helped oversee construction of the Brooklyn Bridge.
The Manhattan Bridge opened in 1909.
The Williamsburg Bridge opened in 1903.
The Queensboro Bridge opened in 1909.
The Queensboro Bridge connects Manhattan and Queens.
The Queensboro Bridge is also known as the 59th Street Bridge.
The Queensboro Bridge passes over Roosevelt Island.
The George Washington Bridge connects Manhattan with New Jersey.
The George Washington Bridge opened in 1931.
The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge connects Brooklyn and Staten Island.
The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge opened in 1964.
The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge was the world's longest suspension bridge when it opened.
The NYC subway began service in 1904.
The first NYC subway line ran from City Hall to 145th Street.
The NYC subway operates 24 hours a day.
The NYC subway serves Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and the Bronx.
Staten Island does not have a traditional NYC subway line.
The Staten Island Railway operates separately from the NYC subway.
The G train is the only NYC subway service that does not enter Manhattan.
The 7 train connects Manhattan with Flushing in Queens.
The L train crosses the East River through the Canarsie Tunnel.
The J and Z trains cross the Williamsburg Bridge.
The N, Q, R, and W trains cross the Manhattan Bridge.
The 4, 5, and 6 trains use the Lexington Avenue corridor.
Grand Central Terminal opened in 1913.
Grand Central Terminal's main concourse has a famous celestial ceiling.
The Grand Central celestial ceiling originally depicted the zodiac sky incorrectly.
Grand Central Terminal has a four-faced clock above its information booth.
Grand Central Terminal contains a hidden tennis court.
Grand Central's Whispering Gallery is famous for its unusual acoustics.
The original Pennsylvania Station was demolished in the 1960s.
Madison Square Garden sits above the current Pennsylvania Station complex.
Rockefeller Center was built during the Great Depression.
Rockefeller Center contains 19 commercial buildings.
The Rockefeller Center Christmas tree tradition began in 1931.
The Rockefeller Center ice rink opened in 1936.
Radio City Music Hall opened in 1932.
The Rockettes were founded in 1925.
30 Rockefeller Plaza is commonly known as 30 Rock.
NBC broadcasts from Rockefeller Center.
The Metropolitan Museum of Art opened in 1870.
The Met is located along Fifth Avenue beside Central Park.
The American Museum of Natural History was founded in 1869.
The American Museum of Natural History is located on the Upper West Side.
The Hayden Planetarium is part of the American Museum of Natural History.
The Museum of Modern Art is commonly known as MoMA.
MoMA opened in 1929.
The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum opened in 1959.
The Guggenheim building was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.
The New York Public Library was founded in 1895.
The New York Public Library's main building is on Fifth Avenue at 42nd Street.
The two lion statues outside the New York Public Library are named Patience and Fortitude.
The Rose Main Reading Room is inside the New York Public Library's main building.
The Flatiron Building was completed in 1902.
The Flatiron Building gets its name from its resemblance to a clothes iron.
The Dakota was completed in 1884.
John Lennon lived at the Dakota.
Washington Square Park was once used as a burial ground.
Washington Square Arch was completed in its permanent form in 1892.
SoHo means South of Houston Street.
NoHo means North of Houston Street.
Tribeca is short for Triangle Below Canal Street.
NoLIta is short for North of Little Italy.
Harlem is located in northern Manhattan.
The Harlem Renaissance made Harlem a major center of African American culture.
The Apollo Theater opened at its current location in 1934.
The Apollo Theater is located on 125th Street.
The Bronx is widely recognized as the birthplace of hip-hop culture.
Hip-hop culture emerged in the Bronx during the 1970s.
Yankee Stadium opened at its current location in 2009.
The New York Yankees originally played at the Polo Grounds.
Citi Field is located in Flushing, Queens.
Citi Field opened in 2009.
The New York Mets play their home games at Citi Field.
Flushing Meadows Corona Park hosted the 1939 World's Fair.
Flushing Meadows Corona Park hosted the 1964 World's Fair.
The Unisphere was built for the 1964 World's Fair.
The New York State Pavilion was built for the 1964 World's Fair.
Forest Hills Gardens was developed beginning in 1909.
Forest Hills Gardens was influenced by the garden-city movement.
Forest Hills Stadium opened in 1923.
Forest Hills Stadium hosted the U.S. National Championships before the tournament moved to Flushing Meadows.
The Beatles performed at Forest Hills Stadium.
The Rolling Stones have performed at Forest Hills Stadium.
Roosevelt Island is part of Manhattan.
The Roosevelt Island Tramway opened in 1976.
The Roosevelt Island Tramway connects Roosevelt Island with Manhattan.
Roosevelt Island was formerly known as Welfare Island.
Inwood is Manhattan's northernmost neighborhood.
Inwood Hill Park contains one of Manhattan's last remaining natural forest areas.
The Harlem River separates Manhattan from the Bronx.
The Harlem River is a tidal strait rather than a conventional river.
Fort Tryon Park is home to The Met Cloisters.
The Met Cloisters is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
The Cloisters specializes in medieval European art and architecture.
The High Line was built on a former elevated freight railroad.
The High Line opened as a public park in 2009.
The High Line runs along Manhattan's West Side.
Hudson Yards is home to The Vessel.
The Vessel opened in 2019.
The Edge observation deck is located at Hudson Yards.
The Bronx Zoo opened in 1899.
The New York Botanical Garden was founded in 1891.
Pelham Bay Park is the largest public park in New York City.
Prospect Park was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux.
Prospect Park opened in the 1860s.
Brooklyn Botanic Garden opened in 1911.
Bowling Green is New York City's oldest public park.
Bowling Green was formally established as a public park in 1733.
Battery Park sits at the southern tip of Manhattan.
Ellis Island served as a major U.S. immigration station from 1892 to 1954.
More than 12 million immigrants were processed through Ellis Island.
The Holland Tunnel opened in 1927.
The Lincoln Tunnel opened in 1937.
The Queens-Midtown Tunnel opened in 1940.
The East River separates Manhattan from Brooklyn and Queens.
The Hudson River separates Manhattan from New Jersey.
Governors Island is located in New York Harbor south of Manhattan.
The Commissioners' Plan of 1811 established much of Manhattan's street grid.
Fifth Avenue divides Manhattan addresses into east and west.
Park Avenue was originally known as Fourth Avenue.
Columbia University was founded in 1754.
Columbia University was originally called King's College.
New York University was founded in 1831.
Fordham University was founded in 1841.
The United Nations headquarters has been on Manhattan's East River since 1952.
The Woolworth Building opened in 1913.
The Woolworth Building was one of the world's tallest buildings when it opened.
St. Patrick's Cathedral on Fifth Avenue was completed in 1878.
The New York Stock Exchange is located on Wall Street.
The New York Stock Exchange traces its origins to the Buttonwood Agreement of 1792.
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held in New York City since 1924.
Arthur Avenue in the Bronx is famous for its Italian-American food culture.
City Island is a nautical community in the Bronx.
Van Cortlandt Park is one of New York City's largest parks.
The Staten Island Ferry operates between Manhattan and Staten Island.
The Staten Island Ferry is free to ride.
The Staten Island Ferry provides views of the Statue of Liberty and Lower Manhattan.
Rockaway Beach is New York City's largest public ocean beach.
Coney Island has been a major amusement destination for more than a century.
The Cyclone roller coaster opened in 1927.
The Cyclone is a designated New York City landmark.
Carnegie Hall opened in 1891.
Carnegie Hall is located near Seventh Avenue and 57th Street.
Lincoln Center opened in the 1960s.
The U.S. Open has been held at Flushing Meadows since 1978.
Arthur Ashe Stadium is located at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.
New York City has hosted the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for more than a century.
New York City's five boroughs were consolidated into one city government in 1898.
Brooklyn was an independent city before the 1898 consolidation.
Long Island City was an independent city before becoming part of New York City in 1898.
Brooklyn takes its name from the Dutch town of Breukelen.
The Bronx is named after Jonas Bronck, a 17th-century settler.
Queens was named for Catherine of Braganza, queen consort of King Charles II.
Staten Island was named after the States General of the Dutch Republic.
Manhattan's name comes from a Lenape place name recorded by European settlers.
New York City has more than 8 million residents.
New York City is the most populous city in the United States.
New York City is home to one of the world's largest public transportation systems.
The MTA operates New York City's subway system.
The MTA also operates Metro-North Railroad and Long Island Rail Road.
Grand Central Madison provides Long Island Rail Road service beneath Grand Central Terminal.
New York City's subway system uses both numbered and lettered services.
New York City has public beaches along the Atlantic Ocean.
Jacob Riis Park is located on the Rockaway Peninsula.
Orchard Beach is located in the Bronx.
New York City has been called the City That Never Sleeps.
